sections.h2: What does the Richland County Recorder of Deeds do?
sections.html:
The Richland County Recorder keeps the public record of who owns land in the county and which liens and mortgages sit on it. The office is at 50 Park Avenue East in Mansfield, Ohio 44902, open Monday through Friday from 8:00 AM to 4:00 PM, and it stops accepting documents for recording at 3:45 PM. The phone is 419-774-5602.

The county's own recorder page traces the job back to 1787, when the Northwest Territory set up a recorder in every county. Ohio became a state in 1803, the post turned elective in 1829, and the term was set at four years in 1936. Today the office indexes each document so a title examiner can build a chain of title from one owner to the next, and the page says the recorder enforces more than 1,000 sections of the Ohio Revised Code.

For a seller in Richland County, the recorder is the last stop. Once the buyer's deed is recorded, the transfer becomes part of the public record.

sections.h2: How do I record a deed in Richland County, step by step?
sections.html:
Deeds pass through several county offices before they are recorded. A typical sequence looks like this.

  • Sign and acknowledge the deed. Section 5301.01 of the Revised Code requires the grantor to sign and to acknowledge the signing before a judge, a clerk of a court of record, a county auditor, a county engineer, a notary public or a mayor.
  • Request tax map pre-approval by email to taxmap@richlandcountyoh.gov. The recorder's page says pre-approval must be included with any electronic deed transfer for real estate.
  • Take the deed to the County Auditor for the conveyance statement and endorsement, and pay the conveyance fee and any county transfer tax.
  • Present the endorsed deed to the Recorder, with the recording fee, before the 3:45 PM cutoff.

The recorder now accepts deed transfers electronically, but any document that needs review by the Tax Map Office and the Auditor must be delivered in person to the courthouse. The office also says it does not provide legal forms, and it urges people to speak to an attorney for help with drafting.

sections.h2: Why does the Richland County Tax Map Office look at my deed?
sections.html:
The Tax Map Office is a division of the Richland County Engineer's Office, and it keeps the property map for every deeded parcel for the auditor. Its services include checking all recorded deeds, maintaining current maps with ownership, providing copies of surveys and checking surveys done in the county. Its collection of tax maps reaches back to 1853 and includes old road record books from the early 1800s. The office phone is 419-774-5620 and it is open weekdays from 8:00 AM to 4:00 PM.

Because the office checks deeds against its maps, a seller who is splitting a lot or changing a legal description should raise it with tax map staff before the closing date.

sections.h2: What does the Auditor require before a deed is recorded in Richland County?
sections.html:
Under section 319.202 of the Revised Code, the buyer or the buyer's representative must file a statement declaring the value of the property before the auditor endorses the deed. The statement carries two affirmations. One covers whether the seller's taxes are reduced by the homestead or owner occupancy programs. The other covers whether the land was in current agricultural use valuation, because land leaving CAUV can owe a recoupment charge under section 5713.34.

The grantor pays the conveyance fee under section 319.54(G)(3). If the county commissioners have levied a transfer tax under Chapter 322, the grantor pays that too. Section 322.02 allows a county rate of up to thirty cents per hundred dollars of value, paid to the auditor at the time the deed is delivered and before it is presented to the recorder. The Richland County Treasurer's page adds that conveyance fees are paid at the treasurer's office. Ask the Auditor which amounts apply to your sale before you schedule a closing.

The statute defines value as the full consideration paid or to be paid, including any mortgage or vendor's lien, and warns that no one may knowingly falsify the value.

sections.h2: What does Richland County charge to record a document?
sections.html:
Recording fees are set by Ohio law. Section 317.32 of the Revised Code lists a base fee of seventeen dollars for the first two pages plus a housing trust fund fee of seventeen dollars, then four dollars base plus four dollars housing trust fund for each added page. A county may also add a document preservation surcharge of up to five dollars. Certified copies and photocopies carry their own per-page charges under the same section.

Page count changes the total, so confirm the exact amount for your document with the recorder's office. Call 419-774-5602 for the current figure before you send a payment.

sections.h2: How do I search Richland County land records?
sections.html:
The recorder's page links to an online records search, and anyone can look up deeds, mortgages and releases to see the chain of title on a house. This is useful for a seller checking whether an old mortgage was ever released, or whether a prior owner's lien is still on file.

The auditor's property search adds parcel data, and the Land Bank at 50 Park Avenue East, lower level 1, acquires vacant and abandoned properties. Anyone selling an inherited house should confirm that the last recorded deed names the person who holds title.

sections.h2: Do older Richland County deeds without witnesses still count?
sections.html:
Usually yes. Section 5301.01(B) treats a deed signed before February 1, 2002 as properly executed even if it was not witnessed by two people as the earlier law required, unless fraud tainted the signature. Recording such an instrument in the county where the land lies is constructive notice to later buyers and lenders, whether it was recorded before, on or after that date.

This rule helps owners who inherited a house with a family deed from decades ago. It does not fix a missing acknowledgment on a deed signed today, so a current deed still needs the notary or other officer named in the statute.

sections.h2: Who decides whether Richland County charges a transfer tax?
sections.html: The board of county commissioners does. Under section 322.02, a county may levy a real property transfer tax by resolution, after two public hearings held three to ten days apart with newspaper, website or public notice sites carrying notice for two consecutive weeks. The resolution is subject to referendum unless adopted as an emergency measure by a unanimous vote. The commissioners may also send the question to voters, and then it takes effect only if a majority approves. Because the rate is a county choice, the figure can differ from one Ohio county to the next, and a seller should not rely on a number from a neighboring county.

sections.h2: What does the Richland County housing stock mean for deed work?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau counts 54,904 housing units and 124,893 residents for 2025, with 114 building permits issued that year. Median monthly owner costs run $1,218 with a mortgage and $489 without one, and 87.6% of residents lived in the same house a year earlier.

Land in Richland County stretches from Mansfield, Ontario and Shelby to villages such as Bellville, Lexington and Plymouth, and into townships named Springfield, Troy, Weller and Worthington.

faqs.q: Where is the Richland County Recorder located?
faqs.a: The office is at 50 Park Avenue East in Mansfield, Ohio 44902. It is open Monday through Friday from 8:00 AM to 4:00 PM, and document recording ends at 3:45 PM. The phone is 419-774-5602.

faqs.q: Do I need tax map approval before recording a deed in Richland County?
faqs.a: Yes for electronic deed transfers. The recorder's page says tax map pre-approval must come with the deed and gives taxmap@richlandcountyoh.gov as the address to request it.

faqs.q: Can I record a Richland County deed online?
faqs.a: The office accepts deed transfers electronically, but documents that need Tax Map and Auditor review must be delivered in person. Call 419-774-5602 to confirm which route fits your document.

faqs.q: Who pays the conveyance fee on a Richland County sale?
faqs.a: The grantor, meaning the seller. Section 319.202 puts the conveyance fee and any county transfer tax on the grantor, paid before the deed goes to the recorder.

faqs.q: Does the Richland County Recorder provide legal forms?
faqs.a: No. The office states that it does not provide legal forms and encourages people to consult an attorney.
